faults.quote: You mentioned 22.5 months for Starter. What monthly amount did you divide the $900 by, and does that match how lifetime value is defined?
faults.why: The candidate had already redone 22.5 as $900 ÷ $30 = 30 months at t11. Probing it again is stale, and the candidate had to point out it was already fixed.

faults.quote: I'm putting up an exhibit: Quillpath — New customers per month, by plan (average per month). What stands out to you in this exhibit?
faults.why: At t15 the candidate asked whether the upgraders would have bought Pro directly anyway. It got no release, refusal or deferral, even though why_pro_fell, buyer_profile and upgrade_timing bear on it. It was only answered after a re-ask at t17.

faults.quote: I'm putting up an exhibit: Quillpath — New customers per month, by plan (average per month).
faults.why: Exhibit-3's figures (500 Pro; 350 Pro + 1,000 Starter) had already gone out as a data line at t8. They were put up again as if new, in place of an answer to the candidate's question.

faults.quote: On the 43%: how did you get to 150 over 350, and which base is right for sizing how much Pro demand moved to Starter?
faults.why: The checker marked the 150 ÷ 350 = 43% claim, framed as a share of today's Pro demand, as correct. The interviewer challenged it as a wrong base, and the candidate retracted a valid figure.

faults.quote: trade-downs were only 30% of Starter sign-ups against the 500 Pro baseline
faults.why: The 150 trade-downs are 30% of the 500 Pro baseline but only 15% of Starter sign-ups. The line puts the 30% on the wrong quantity.

faults.quote: How would you guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's last answer already gave the protection: a partial rollout, a $40 control for nine months, and gating rollout on the upgrade rate. The follow-up re-asks what was just covered.

faults.quote: How would you guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's sensitivity netted $640,000 instead of $600,000, because it used the $130k trade-down loss with a $1,100 net per sign-up. On that basis they set a 15% upgrade tripwire, but the case's breakeven is 12.5%. Neither figure was probed before the case closed.
